A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MFAI study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the expanded experiments and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original MuSiQue and NeoQA evaluations, attention analyses, and gold-only and no-document ablations in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds evaluations involving 2WikiMultiHopQA, higher-hop questions, a 32B model, distractor changes and instruction-order sensitivity.

M1.justification: The original two-document MFAI prompt and training-free procedure remain. Appendix A.7.2 makes a limited higher-hop adaptation: instructions target three or four documents, and unmatched instructions mirror their indices into an empty bucket selected with T > M > B priority.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual evaluations on the Compositional and Inference subsets of 2WikiMultiHopQA and MuSiQue three- and four-hop questions. It also tests NeoQA with random-timeline distractors instead of only same-timeline distractors, expanding both reasoning requirements and input conditions.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged: No MFAI, matched/unmatched conditions, and gold-only/no-document controls remain. The additional dataset and model-scale studies extend these comparisons; the 32B model is an added experimental configuration.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce sparse distance/index grids, specified higher-hop placements and mirror controls, a quantized 32B configuration tested on the first 600 MuSiQue examples, and a 96-cell instruction-order pilot. The reported heatmap sample increases from 20 to 100 examples, with priority-fill selection specified in v2. The original two-hop dataset sizes and accuracy metrics remain.

E4.justification: v2 adds controlled tests of distractor provenance and instruction-index ordering, a separate MuSiQue attention heatmap, and quantitative thinking-cost analysis. It extends gold-only and no-document ablations to higher hops. The earlier unmatched-variant analysis is retained and consolidated in Appendix A.9.

E5.justification: v2 adds 95% bootstrap confidence intervals using 10,000 resamples to Figures 2–3 and paired McNemar tests covering 72 comparisons in Tables 1–2. Its rewritten attention appendix drops v1's description of standard-error intervals for focus curves. Seed 42 remains fixed; no increase in independent experimental seeds is reported.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive dataset, higher-hop, model-scale, robustness and compute-cost results in Tables 5–16. Retained results also change: Figure 3 reports MuSiQue Ministral-8B Unmatched accuracy for Beginning+Middle as 20.7% in v1 versus 22.69% in v2. The original two-hop gold-only and no-document table values are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix A.5 newly defines paired binary outcomes, the continuity-corrected McNemar statistic and its chi-square null distribution. The weakest-link probability argument and attention aggregation remain substantively unchanged; the rewritten normalization exposition adds no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract qualifies the weakest-link claim by the 18-document, three-bucket setting, while the contributions and conclusion explicitly claim replication across additional datasets, hop counts and model scales. The central account of divergent MFAI effects changes from real-world versus synthetic data to vertical versus horizontal task topology.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the synthetic-data/model-prior explanation with task topology and distractor homogeneity. Section 3.1 acknowledges oracle access and search-space reduction, treating matched-MFAI gains as an upper-bound estimate of recognition difficulty. The limitations additionally acknowledge answer-format confounding and strict-EM sensitivity.

D1.justification: v1 promises future code/data release; v2 supplies a repository link and reports release of code and curated artifacts under a permissive license. It also specifies the heatmap layer range and priority sampler, higher-hop placement rules, quantized checkpoint and token-counting procedure, and documents residual batching nondeterminism.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ho et al. (2020), Efron and Tibshirani (1994), and McNemar (1947) for the new dataset and statistical analyses. The main related-work positioning remains largely intact. Publication and author-metadata corrections concern already cited works.

P1.justification: Substantial rewrites affect the abstract, contributions, unmatched-instruction discussion, conclusion and limitations. Appendix A.4 is condensed and rewritten, and the earlier unmatched-variant specification and analysis are merged into A.9. Terminology changes from 'Law' to 'Effect', alongside widespread language corrections.

P2.justification: v2 adds substantial statistical, validation and robustness tables, expands ablation tables with higher-hop columns, and redraws the main bar charts with confidence intervals and revised overlays/legends. It replaces the displayed attention heatmap and adds a separate MuSiQue heatmap. v1 Figure 7 is retained as v2 Figure 8.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens v1's narrow empirical validation through additional dataset, hop-count and model-scale checks, targeted controls, and statistical uncertainty reporting. It also addresses important interpretation weaknesses by acknowledging MFAI's search-space confound and the datasets' answer-format confound, while improving reproducibility documentation and reporting code/data release. Some categorical causal assertions in Section 4 remain stronger than these qualifications permit, but the broader evidence and clearer limitations provide a substantial net quality improvement.
